PMID:22715424.topic: One-stop wide-awake hand surgery service outcomes
PMID:22715424.setting: Parkside one-stop wide-awake day-case surgical centre (CQC-certified primary care facility adjoined to a GP surgery), Boston, Lincolnshire
PMID:22715424.standard: Service targets: one-stop care, wide-awake care, 0% referral to hospital, low DNA rate, 0% litigation, patient satisfaction >99%, 0% deferral for investigation (locally set)

cycle1.result: Last 1000 consecutive cases: one-stop and wide-awake care achieved in 1000 cases; referral to hospital 0%; DNA rate 0.2%; litigation 0%; patient satisfaction >99%; deferral for investigation 0%; all cases managed within 45 minutes (median 30 minutes); 3 superficial surgical site infections and 15 delayed wound healing cases.

PMID:22715424.intervention: Absorbable skin sutures (introduced early 2011) replaced by non-absorbable silk sutures after audit linked them to infection and delayed wound healing.
PMID:22715424.other_findings: Referral diagnosis was correct in over 90% of cases (97 revised); estimated saving to the NHS of about £750,000 per 1000 cases and a mean wait of four weeks from referral to treatment.

PMID:38274930.topic: Paediatric forearm fracture manipulation in the emergency department
PMID:38274930.setting: Poole Hospital, University Hospitals Dorset NHS Foundation Trust, district general hospital emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics
PMID:38274930.standard: BOAST and GIRFT recommendations that units have protocols for manipulation of paediatric forearm fractures under procedural analgesia in the ED, avoiding admission and general anaesthesia; local standard operating procedure

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation (n=11 suitable fractures): manipulation in ED 1 (9.1%); theatre required 4 (36.4%).

PMID:38274930.intervention: New standard operating procedure and paediatric fracture manipulation pathway in the ED using intranasal fentanyl and Entonox, agreed with ED, orthopaedics, radiology and theatre managers; information leaflets planned after cycle 2.

cycle2.result: Third cycle (n=52): manipulation in ED 9 (17.3%); theatre required 1 (1.9%). All nine manipulable fractures were manipulated in the ED.

PMID:38274930.other_findings: Second cycle (n=74): manipulation in ED 11 (14.9%), theatre required 21 (28.4%); 27% of manipulable fractures were manipulated in ED and none of these later needed theatre. All manipulations were done by the orthopaedic on-call team, none by ED; documentation and consent remained areas for improvement.

PMID:30094343.setting: Trauma and Orthopaedics department, Frimley Park Hospital (750-bed NHS hospital), Surrey
PMID:30094343.standard: 10 handover components derived from RCS, RCP and BMA handover guidelines, each with a set standard (some patient identifiers at 100%); aim to raise compliance to 90–100%

cycle1.result: Baseline (247 handovers over nine weeks): patient name 99%, hospital number 94%, admission reason 91%, other categories 12% to 84% (date of birth 54%, location 84%, frequency of review 70%, TTO 12%); only admission reason met its standard.

PMID:30094343.intervention: Two-step change: extra columns (TTO, day to be seen, DNAR) added to the Word handover table, then a new intranet handover tool with drop-down boxes, date selector and multiuser access; instruction document given at induction.

cycle2.result: Sustainability re-audit of intranet tool (201 handovers, new cohort of doctors): patient name 100%, hospital number 98%, date of birth 85%; five of 10 categories met their standard (patient name, location, consultant, admission reason, frequency of review); all except TTO were above 50%.

PMID:30094343.other_findings: After the amended table (257 handovers) TTO rose from 12% to 31% and location fell from 84% to 77%; after the intranet tool (207 handovers) location 90%, consultant 94%, admission reason 97%, frequency of review 100% and TTO 5%. TTO stayed poorest (18%) and was dropped from the tool.

PMID:34820213.topic: Secondary fracture prevention after hip fracture
PMID:34820213.setting: Orthopaedic wards of a large district general hospital with a level 2 trauma centre
PMID:34820213.standard: Royal College of Physicians National Hip Fracture Database: all patients with hip fracture assessed for and managed with a secondary bone-protection plan (100% gold standard); SMART aim of an additional 40% per year

cycle1.result: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.

PMID:34820213.intervention: PDSA 1 awareness poster (January 2019); PDSA 2 education session for clerking and ward doctors added to induction (March 2019); PDSA 3 MDT meeting with responsibility charting, giving assessment and prescribing to the care of the elderly team (April 2019).

cycle2.dates: April 2019 (a fortnight after the MDT meeting)
cycle2.result: 100% (n=50) of patients assessed or placed on a bone-protection plan.

PMID:34820213.other_findings: PDSA 1 (n=27) 44.4% (p<0.01) and PDSA 2 (n=21) 76% (p<0.001); an annual re-audit of 50 patients during the COVID-19 pandemic showed 100% was sustained. At baseline 89.9% of patients and relatives were unaware of bone protection.

PMID:39664163.standard: Local SMART objective: satisfaction rate of at least 80% among patients assigned to PIFU

cycle1.result: 203 of 3828 fracture clinic patients (5.3%) assigned to PIFU; 183 (90.15%) received the leaflet; 41 (20.2%) used PIFU; 163 (80.3%) rated the service 5/5 and all 203 reported satisfaction, so the 80% target was met.

PMID:39664163.other_findings: 20 PIFU patients (9.85%) did not receive the leaflet; of all clinic attenders 2549 (66.6%) had regular follow-up and 1076 (28.1%) were discharged.

PMID:38111391.setting: Trauma and orthopaedics, single centre (audit approved at University Hospitals Dorset, Poole General Hospital; authors at Dorset County Hospital)
PMID:38111391.standard: BOAST ankle fracture standards and NICE NG37: documentation of mechanism, skin integrity, circulation, neurological examination and repeat neurovascular examination after reduction; target 100%

cycle1.result: Mechanism of injury 86%; skin integrity 54%; circulation status 54%; detailed vascular examination 17%; neurological examination 54%; sensory detail 48%; MRC motor scale 48%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 56%; overall precise documentation of clinical findings 17%.

PMID:38111391.intervention: Targeted education on documentation standards at induction and trauma meetings, with case-based discussion reports; made a permanent part of departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Mechanism of injury 100%; skin integrity 100%; circulation status 88%; detailed vascular examination 88%; neurological examination 88%; sensory detail 88%; MRC motor scale 88%; repeat neurovascular examination after reduction 88%; overall precise documentation 88%.

PMID:38111391.other_findings: Re-audit identified 22 patients, 17 included after exclusions. The shorthand 'DNVI' was the main cause of incomplete records and persisted in two patients after the intervention.

PMID:33973847.topic: Antibiotic prophylaxis duration in spinal surgery
PMID:33973847.setting: Spine Unit, Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery Department, Assiut University Hospitals (tertiary spine centre)
PMID:33973847.standard: North American Spine Society (NASS) 2013 guideline on perioperative antibiotic prophylaxis: preoperative dose, redosing as needed, discontinuation within 24 hours for uncomplicated non-instrumented surgery

cycle1.result: All patients received a correct preoperative first-generation cephalosporin dose, but IV antibiotics continued 1–6 days followed by oral antibiotics until suture removal (up to two weeks) in all patients, with mixed agents; SSI 1 case (1.85%).

PMID:33973847.intervention: New local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol (first-generation cephalosporin 30–60 minutes before incision, redose after 3 hours, stop at 24 hours) agreed in discussion sessions and disseminated by pamphlet and theatre poster.

cycle2.result: All patients received preoperative first-generation cephalosporin continued for only 24 hours postoperatively and were discharged on day 2; no SSI.

PMID:33973847.other_findings: Difference in infection rates was not statistically significant; mean postoperative stay fell from 3.33 to 2.04 days.

PMID:41111789.setting: Plastic Surgery Department, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust (tertiary centre)
PMID:41111789.standard: BSSH hand trauma standards: open fractures/joints and bites within 24 hours, other open injuries within four days, closed fractures within seven days; project target 80% compliance

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 73% (part of national BSSH-RSTN collaborative audit).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 83% (82/99); open soft tissue 97% (32/33); bites 100% (10/10); open fractures/joints 64% (9/14); tendon injuries 76.5% (13/17); closed fractures 67% (16/24), surgical fixation 50% (7/14); median decision-to-surgery time 42.7 hours.

PMID:41111789.other_findings: Theatre capacity caused 52% (9/17) of delays and front-end referral problems 28% (5/17). Recommendations include more trauma list capacity, expanded 52 Pre-Op clinic and MIU, education for referring units and rolling audits.

PMID:26623160.setting: Hip fracture unit, James Cook University Hospital, Middlesbrough
PMID:26623160.standard: Hip fracture best practice tariff: surgery within 36 hours of admission

cycle1.result: Warfarinised patients on oral vitamin K protocol: mean time to theatre 53.71 hours; 79% breached BPT due to anticoagulation.

PMID:26623160.intervention: Nurse-led 'early trigger' protocol giving 2 mg intravenous vitamin K in the emergency department before the INR result, added to the fast-track pathway.

cycle2.result: Mean time to theatre 37.61 hours (p<0.0001); 34% breached BPT due to anticoagulation; 21 (50%) operated within 36 hours and 33 (79%) within 48 hours.

PMID:26623160.other_findings: No thromboembolic complications or deaths attributed to the protocol; 10 patients were delayed purely by inadequate reversal. Non-warfarinised controls (n=403) had mean time to theatre 28.36 hours.

PMID:38024025.setting: Orthopaedic trauma list, St Richard's Hospital, district general hospital, Chichester
PMID:38024025.standard: RCN, AAGBI, European Society of Anaesthesiology and ASA guidelines: fasting of two hours for clear fluids and six hours for solids

cycle1.result: All 50 patients (100%) fasted beyond six hours for solids (mean 15.8 hours, range 9–24) and 49 (98%) beyond two hours for clear fluids (mean 10.5 hours, range 2–20); only 5 (10%) had correct documented fasting instructions; 31 (62%) were 'nil by mouth from midnight'.

PMID:38024025.other_findings: Staff survey showed poor knowledge: only 42.9% of ward nurses knew the 6 hour/2 hour rule. Only 52% received preoperative IV fluids; a 'sip till send' policy has since been introduced.

PMID:41257126.setting: University Hospitals Dorset, large district general hospital (emergency department, orthopaedics and virtual fracture clinic)
PMID:41257126.standard: Local UHD Achilles tendon rupture pathway: VTE prophylaxis, boot with wedges, non-weight-bearing advice, ultrasound within 14 days and virtual fracture clinic referral; target 100%

cycle1.result: VTE prophylaxis 110/138 (80%); boot immobilisation 110/138 (80%); ultrasound within 14 days 59/138 (43%); non-weight-bearing advice 91/138 (66%); VFC referral 132/138 (96%).

PMID:41257126.intervention: Results emailed with recommendations, pathway posters displayed in ED, orthopaedic team room and fracture clinic, and a new 'Ultrasound Achilles' imaging request form.

cycle2.result: VTE prophylaxis 35/44 (80.5%, p=0.91); boot immobilisation 38/44 (86%, p=0.04); ultrasound within 14 days 26/44 (59%, p=0.03); non-weight-bearing advice 29/44 (66%, p=0.99); VFC referral 44/44 (100%, p=0.01).

PMID:41257126.other_findings: VTE prophylaxis and weight-bearing advice did not improve. No re-ruptures or VTE events in either cycle.

PMID:10247653.topic: Neomycin irrigation use in orthopaedic surgery
